## Intent

- Orchestration reads text in two ways today: a script matches a pattern, or an agent spends turns reading. The first misses what needs comprehension; the second is slow, costly and unrecorded.
- Jev (`~/.claude/skills/asking-jev/`) returns a typed answer with a probability in under a second: `noul`, `choice`, `score`. Nothing under `scripts/` or `.claude/skills/` calls it yet (grep, 2026-09-17).
- Wanted: every judgment in the base's orchestration that Jev fits is a Jev call behind the script that already owns that reading. Code keeps the workflow, the exact lookups and the refusals.
- SDLC readings (`spec/sdlc`, `check-sdlc-tie`) are out: sdlc-alloy#244's.

## Definition of done

- One table on this issue: every candidate reading, its owner script, the question type, and adopt or reject with the reason.
- One shared caller, key from `~/.env`, the answering `model` pinned, and a named fallback when the call fails: the script answers `unknown`, never a guess.
- Each adopted reading has cases from this tracker's own history, one fitting no option, asserted as a band; its threshold is set by the cost of acting wrongly.
- A Jev answer never allows a write on its own: it warns, ranks or routes, and a refusal stays with deterministic code.
- Every call logs what it read, the answer and the branch taken.

## Plan

| step | what |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Survey candidates, as a `NOTE` here; the seeds are this issue's first `NOTE`. |
| 2 | Planner picks by measured cost, per rule-check#275. |
| 3 | Shared caller and its test. |
| 4 | Adopt one reading per pull request, costliest first. |

- Driven a step at a time by the planner; each step ends in a `NOTE`.
- All independent questions over one state go in one call.

state.body:
Campaign: kalaluthien/campaign-base#1
Repository: kalaluthien/campaign-base

`scripts/campaign-assign.py` (landed by #198) answers "has this pane compacted since its last release" by reading the pane's text. **A pane's text holds what it has DISPLAYED as well as what it printed**, and `herdr agent read <pane>` puts another session's output into the reader's own scrollback — which `AGENTS.md` § Watching and retiring makes the ordinary planner move.

So a planner that released its own claim and then read a delegate's pane has, in its own scrollback and in this order: a release anchor, and the delegate's compaction marker. Found by review at e680ef8 and reproduced through the real module: verdict `compacted`, at line 4.

#198 closed half of it. The anchor `campaign-claim: released <branch> in <pane>` now names the pane it was printed in, so a *release* copied from elsewhere is not this pane's. **The marker cannot be qualified that way** — `Compacted (ctrl+o to see full summary)` is harness UI text with nothing in it that says whose pane it is. So the residue is: this pane's own release, followed by somebody else's marker read into this pane, reads `compacted`. It ASSIGNS, which is the wrong direction.

The bound on it: the planner's own compaction must have failed first (or it would carry its own marker), and it must then read another pane before being assigned. Narrow, but it is the exact case the guard exists for.

## The work

**Stop reading the pane; read the session's own transcript.** `~/.claude/projects/<slugged-cwd>/<session>.jsonl` is the session's record rather than a rendering of one, and nothing another pane displays can enter it. `scripts/campaign-token-tally.py` (#195) already reads that tree and knows its shape, so the reader exists.

1. **Probe first, and write the result into the docstring with the date:** what a compaction writes into the transcript. Whether there is a record type, a `isCompactSummary`-style flag, or only a boundary inferable from the token counts. If there is no durable marker, say so and stop — the answer changes what can be built, and an inferred boundary is not a measurement.
2. Resolve pane → session id through `herdr agent list` (`agent_session.value`, which `campaign-claim.py`'s `parse_agents` already reads), then session id → transcript path.
3. Replace `compaction_verdict`'s pane reading with the transcript reading, keeping the three verdicts and both flags. Keep every could-not-look explicit: no transcript, an unreadable one, and a session id no row names are three different absences and all three refuse.
4. Retire what the pane reading needed and the transcript does not: `MARKER`, `GUTTER`, `rendered`, `READ_CAP`, `--lines`, and the measurements behind them. Sweep #198's cases for the ones that only exist to defend the substring match.

## Done when

The pull request is merged; `campaign-assign` decides from the transcript; a case shows that another pane's marker read into this pane does not admit it; and the probe from step 1 is recorded with its date and its raw output.

## Working it

This body is the whole brief, so this section is here on every sub-issue. It
points rather than restates: the rules are in the base's `AGENTS.md`, which a
delegate reaches through the `--add-dir <base>` its launch passes, and a second
copy of them here would be the one that goes stale.

- **A branch is already claimed on the remote for this sub-issue.** Its name is
  not written here — `gh issue create` mints the issue number, so the branch
  cannot be named in the body that creates it, and a placeholder nobody fills is
  worse than an absence. Read it with
  `scripts/campaign-claim.py live <N>`, which lists every claim of the campaign
  and where each is checked out. Check it out and work on it, and push every
  commit the moment it exists — a checkout that dies costs uncommitted work and
  nothing more.
- **Land by pull request against `main`**, opened on the first commit, body
  closing this issue with `Closes kalaluthien/campaign-base#<issue>`. Merge
  `origin/main` in before merging; resolve on the branch, never force-push.
- **You may land your own work**, and the three conditions that gate it are
  `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions. One of them is a review you did not write, so
  **commission it yourself**: an in-process subagent, always, with the model and
  the level named — `AGENTS.md` § Review, and
  `.claude/skills/opening-campaign/references/reviewing.md` for the call.
- **The four messages** are `AGENTS.md` § The four messages. `REPORT` once when
  the pull request is open, unsolicited, naming its URL and the sha it sits at,
  **and ask for the review there**: a push retires any review before it and
  nobody is named to notice. If you ask and nothing comes, say so and stop — a
  silent wait reads exactly like work.
- **A fix round** is `AGENTS.md` § The fix round: reproduce each finding at the
  site it names before touching anything, and close the round with one `REPORT`
  plus a comment at that sha carrying one row per finding.
- **You do not write the campaign issue's body.** It is written at a scope
  change and at the close, and a sub-issue is neither.

A sub-issue pays a fixed cost — an issue, a claim, a branch, a pull request and at least one review round — and measured over 2026-09-04T00:45Z–2026-09-05T01:00Z (`campaign-token-tally.py`, method on #195, tally on #1) that floor swamps a small patch. #171 landed 21 changed lines and its one review round alone cost 57,374 input tokens: 2,732 input tokens per changed line, against 668 for #177 (3,164 lines) and 674 for #187 (1,723 lines). #170 came to 1,771 per line on 53 lines. The measurement also found the reason the floor cannot be read off the cheap sub-issues in full: #169, #170 and #171 were worked at the base root on `main`, with no worktree and no claim branch checked out, so nothing in the transcript ties their implementation turns to them. Campaign: kalaluthien/agent-workspace#1

**The documented liveness check reports a live session as dead**, and it is the
reading two destructive gates rest on.

```sh
kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && [ "$(ps -o comm= -p "$PID")" = claude ]
```

`ps -o comm=` does not return a fixed string. Measured 2026-08-29 against two
`claude` processes running side by side on this machine:

| pid | `ps -o comm=` | the test says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 79873 | `claude` | alive |
| 24840 | `/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe` | **dead** |

Both were live campaign sessions of campaign #1 at the moment of the reading, and
`kill -0` returned success for both. What differs is how each was launched, which
nothing in the record distinguishes and no reader can see.

**Why this is worse than a wrong answer.** The comparison is documented as
erring towards refusing to take over — "a recycled PID belonging to a *different*
`claude` reads as live, so the check errs towards refusing" (`AGENTS.md` § Who is
a campaign session). This defect errs the other way, which is the direction that
destroys work:

- `closing-campaign` step 1 sweeps `runtime/executors/` and reads each record's
  pid this way. A live executor whose `comm` is the full path reads as dead, so
  the no-live-agent gate passes and the close deletes the tree under a session
  that is working in it.
- `closing-campaign` step 0 and `opening-campaign` step 1 decide holder takeover
  the same way. A session arriving to a *live* holder reads it as dead and
  overwrites `runtime/holder`, giving one campaign two holders — the state the
  file exists to make impossible.

Two executor sessions of campaign #1 are live under this record right now, and
both read as dead.

Four sites carry the comparison: `AGENTS.md:95`,
`.claude/skills/opening-campaign/SKILL.md:101`,
`.claude/skills/closing-campaign/SKILL.md:97`, and
`.claude/skills/closing-campaign/SKILL.md:129`.

The work:

1. Replace the equality with one that holds for every launch shape — match the
   basename against `claude` and `claude.exe`, or whatever a probe shows the set
   to be. Probe before choosing: the two shapes above are what this machine
   happens to be running today, not a proof that there are only two.
2. Apply it at all four sites. A liveness reading that differs between the open
   and the close is the drift this repository refuses everywhere else, so
   consider whether the four prose copies should become one script the way
   `campaign-repos` and `campaign-settlement` did.
3. Keep the direction of the residual error stated where the check is defined:
   a recycled pid still reads as live, and that is the safe direction. Say so,
   because the next person to tighten this will otherwise re-introduce the
   defect while making the check "stricter".
4. Check whether `scripts/campaign-local-work` performs the same reading, and
   fix it there too if so.

Ordering: this is independent of #57, #59, #60 and #62 in the sections it edits,
except that #59 rewrites the surrounding liveness prose. It should land **first**
— the hazard is live today, and #59 will take several phases, so #59 inherits
whatever lands here rather than the reverse.

Done when the pull request is merged, and the fixed check has been run against
two live `claude` processes with different `comm` shapes and reported both alive.

state.body:
## Intent

Bring the container's herdr layer up to what herdr now is. Our practice was written against herdr 0.8.0 and against reading the screen: `AGENTS.md` tells a session to type a launch line, send the prompt separately, read the pane once, and infer a delegate's state from a screen that reports `idle` for a session sitting on a dialog. herdr 0.8.2 answers those same questions directly — `agent prompt` refuses an agent already at an approval or question dialog with `agent_blocked` instead of sending text into it, and `agent start` waits for the new shell and first-run prompt to be ready instead of reporting premature readiness — and a Claude state hook (`herdr-agent-state.sh`) this machine has never installed would replace screen-guessing with reported state.

Every one of those rules is prose with no reader. The container has learned twice what that costs: the settlement rule drifted into `gh` commands until `scripts/campaign-settlement` became its one reader, and the `## Repos` rule had drifted into three prose copies before `scripts/campaign-repos` was written. The herdr recipes are the last block of that kind, and the one whose facts go stale fastest, because the tool underneath them keeps moving. One guard runs the other way: the official herdr skill says never to drive panes when `HERDR_ENV` is unset, our documents have never said it, and a session running outside a pane can drive another session today.

So: measure what the installed binary and the state hook actually do, retire the workarounds the tool has absorbed, keep the ones that still hold with the measurement that keeps them, and leave the launch-and-liveness recipe as something a session runs rather than something it reads and retypes.

## Scope

In:

- `scripts/` — where a herdr recipe becomes a reader, in the shape `campaign-settlement` and `campaign-repos` already set.
- `AGENTS.md` § Delegating to a repository agent, § What silently stops a delegate before it starts, and the liveness half of § Completion and liveness — the rule stays, the mechanics move to the reader.
- `AGENTS.md` § Naming a session, and the naming of live sessions on this machine. Added 2026-08-30 on the owner's word, with #88 moved here from #1: a session's two names are a herdr pane name and a harness name, neither propagating to the other, so the rule is a herdr fact before it is a campaign rule and its consumer is `scripts/campaign-name-session`.
- `.claude/skills/` only where a skill repeats a recipe the script now owns.
- `setup-herdr.md` in this container's memory pool: every item re-measured against the installed version and kept with its evidence, corrected, or retired.
- The installed herdr itself: which version this machine runs, and whether the Claude state hook is installed.

Out:

- herdr's own source. That repository is not ours; a finding that argues for changing it is filed upstream or recorded, never acted on here.
- `~/workspace/scripts/` — `herdr-survey` and `herdr-update` stay as they are. A change there is a separate piece of work in that repository.
- Campaign machinery that is not about driving herdr. That is #1's scope, and this campaign files anything it finds there as a subtask of #1 rather than doing it.

## Requirements

- The report names the herdr version every measurement was taken against, and that version is the one installed on this machine at the time.
- Every item surviving in `setup-herdr.md` carries the command that measured it and the version it was measured against; every item retired names the release that absorbed it.
- No rule left in `AGENTS.md`'s delegate or liveness sections rests on a claim that does not reproduce against the installed version.
- The launch-and-liveness mechanics have exactly one reader under `scripts/`, and no second copy of them survives in `AGENTS.md` or either skill — a grep for the retired mechanics returns nothing.
- `AGENTS.md` states when a session may drive a pane at all, and names what makes that answerable rather than assumed.
- A claim that a herdr behaviour changed is backed by a live probe, never by a release note alone.

## Repos

- kalaluthien/agent-workspace

Campaign: kalaluthien/agent-workspace#61

The official herdr skill requires `test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1` before any control command, and tells an agent that fails the check to say it is not running inside herdr and stop. No document in this container states that guard — and #63's inventory (row 88) surfaced why stating it is not a one-line edit: a campaign session runs `herdr agent list`, `agent start` and `pane read` routinely, and it is not a delegate inside a pane. Written literally into `AGENTS.md`, the guard forbids the container's own daily path; written as an exception for "the campaign session", it is a rule that exempts whoever is reading it.

So the question this subtask answers is not "state the guard" but which of three the guard actually is here:

- a guard for a *delegate*, which must not reach outside its pane and drive its siblings — in which case the campaign session is out of its scope by construction and the exemption is not an exemption;
- a guard for any *agent* issuing control commands, in which case the campaign session is in breach today and something has to change;
- moot for a non-agent CLI caller, in which case it belongs in the herdr layer's notes and not in `AGENTS.md` at all.

- Read the guard's own wording in the bundled skill (`herdr --skill`) and, if they differ, in `herdrdev/herdr`'s `skills/herdr/SKILL.md` on master. The wording is the evidence; do not settle this from memory of it.
- Establish what `HERDR_ENV` is actually set to in each of the three places that matter here: a delegate launched into a pane, a campaign session in a pane, and a session with no pane at all. That is a probe, not a reading — a rule written against an assumed value is the failure this campaign exists to stop.
- Decide which of the three readings holds, and write the consequence where the decision is made rather than where it is remembered: `AGENTS.md` if a session must check something, the herdr layer's notes if it must not.
- If the second reading holds, say plainly what changes; do not soften it into a note.

Depends on nothing else in #61 and blocks nothing, so it can run at any point.

Done when the pull request is merged, or — if the answer is that nothing in this container should change — when this issue is closed as completed with the probe results and the reasoning in a comment.

state.body:
Campaign: #1 (kalaluthien/agent-workspace).

## What happened

The interactive session in pane `w40:p11` was named `campaign-1-executor-1` while
it worked campaign #1. It then opened campaign #116, bound it, scaffolded
`retire-workspace-board-260902/`, filed its sub-issues and launched a delegate
`campaign-116-executor-1` — the whole time still called `campaign-1-executor-1`.
Nothing noticed. It was renamed by hand afterwards.

## Cause: no step sets the name, and no reader checks it

**1. Nothing in the opening procedure names the session.**
`.claude/skills/opening-campaign/SKILL.md` has six steps and none of them
mentions the name. `campaign-name-session.py` is referenced from exactly one
procedural place in the tree — `references/launching.md:21-23` — and that is
about `--name`ing a *delegate* at launch, not about the launching session's own
name. The join path, SKILL.md:58-63 ("No directory at all"), lists steps 2, 4 and
5 and is likewise silent. So the name is set only when a person or a session
thinks to set it.

**2. No reader ever compares the name to the campaign.**
`AGENTS.md:107` requires the *binding* be read before every anchor write and
every launch; `AGENTS.md:124` states the name rule. Nothing joins the two.
`campaign-name-session.py:46` validates only the *shape*
(`^campaign-[0-9]+-executor-[0-9]+$`) — `campaign-1-executor-1` is a perfectly
valid name — and it is the rule's only consumer (its own header, lines 11-14).
The sharpest instance: `campaign-claim.py take` receives the anchor as its first
positional (`scripts/campaign-claim.py:722`) and the name as `--name`
(`:725`), and `write_record` (`:240-256`) writes the name verbatim with no
comparison to the anchor and no shape check. The same file already contains the
sibling check for the *branch* — `stray_branches` (`:615-621`) flags a record
whose branch is not under `campaign-<anchor>/` — so the precedent exists and the
name was simply left out of it.

**3. `opening-campaign` propagates the stale name.**
SKILL.md:215 tells the claim step to pass `--name "<this session's ListAgents
name>"`, i.e. whatever the name currently is. A stale name is copied into the
durable record by the procedure itself.

## What a stale name breaks, and what it does not

Breaks:
- **Human and peer routing.** `herdr agent list` and `ListAgents` are how a
  person tells one campaign's sessions from another's on one machine. A session
  filing #116's issues under `campaign-1-executor-1` is invisible as #116's and
  looks like a #1 session doing out-of-scope work.
- **The claim record's address.** `campaign-claim.py list` prints `name` as the
  address to reach the holder (`:384-385`); a record under #116 naming
  `campaign-1-executor-1` sends the next reader to look for a #1 session.
- **The delegate's brief.** The launched `campaign-116-executor-1` was told its
  launcher is `campaign-1-executor-1`, so a `BLOCKED` or `REPORT` addressed back
  by name names a session that, to any observer, belongs to another campaign.

Does not break:
- **`campaign-claim live`.** It joins records to `herdr agent list` on the
  harness **session id** and on nothing else, deliberately (`:598-604`,
  `:665-672`). A rename or a stale name cannot move a row between its three
  groups.
- **Any gate.** The binding (`campaign-tracker bound`), the claim
  (create-ref), settlement, and the close gates all read GitHub, the remote or
  the session id. None reads the name, so nothing was mis-gated — which is
  exactly why this ran for a whole campaign without a symptom.

## The spec assumes one session, one campaign

`spec/alloy/session.als` gives `Session` no name at all — `sig Session` is
`smach`, `holds`, `surveyResult`, `readme`, `bodyAsRead`, `claims`
(`session.als:24-31`). The name is unmodelled, so no invariant could have tied it
to anything.

More to the point, the model forbids the transition that happened. Both ways a
session acquires a campaign are preconditioned on holding none:

    pred adopt[s: Session, c: Campaign] {
      c in Filed and c.anchor in Open
      no s.holds                                    -- session.als:94

    pred sFileAnchor[s: Session] {
      ...
      no s.holds                                    -- session.als:130

and no event anywhere clears `holds` — every other predicate carries
`holds' = holds`. So in the model a session belongs to exactly one campaign for
its entire life, and the name being a constant is consistent with that. Reality
is not: one interactive session outlived campaign #1's active phase and opened
#116. The name rule was written for the modelled world.

## Options

**A. `opening-campaign` names the session.** Add a step: immediately after the
anchor number exists (end of step 3), and on the "no directory" join path
(step 1), run `scripts/campaign-name-session.py <own pane> campaign-<N>-executor-<n>`
and confirm with `ListAgents` before continuing.
*For:* fixes the cause at the one moment the number is first known; costs one
command. *Against:* it is a procedure step, the class of rule this repository
says to mechanise; the caller's own rename is the one most likely to need a
person (`campaign-name-session.py:27-33`), so the step must report an honest
failure rather than assume success; and it does not cover a session that joins a
campaign through the routing gate without running the skill.

**B. `campaign-claim.py take` refuses a name from another campaign.** Compare
`--name`'s `campaign-<M>-` against the `<N>` positional and refuse when they
disagree, alongside the existing `stray_branches` check.
*For:* deterministic, testable in `campaign-claim-test.py`, and it fires at the
moment a stale name would enter a durable record — the only place a stale name
does lasting damage. *Against:* partial. This session never claimed for #116
(it launched a delegate), so B alone would not have caught this incident.

**C. Drop the campaign number: `executor-<n>`.** Remove the falsifiable field, so
nothing can go stale.
*For:* no rule left to break. *Against:* the number is the only thing that tells
a person which campaign a pane belongs to when several run on one machine, which
is the name's whole job; and it costs a sweep of `AGENTS.md:124`,
`campaign-name-session.py:46`, `check-rule-readers.py:188-189`, both skills'
references, and every delegate `--name` in flight.

## Recommendation

**A, with B as its second reader.** A is the missing act; B is what keeps it from
drifting back, and this repository's own rule is that a declared contract stays
true only while something on the authoring side enforces it. C is rejected: it
removes the symptom by removing the information.

## Done when

1. `scripts/campaign-claim.py take <N> <issue> <topic> --name campaign-<M>-executor-1`
   with `M != N` exits non-zero and prints a line naming both numbers; a case in
   `scripts/campaign-claim-test.py` fails when that comparison is deleted.
2. `.claude/skills/opening-campaign/SKILL.md` step 3 and the step-1 "No directory
   at all" path each call `campaign-name-session.py` on the session's own pane,
   and a live probe on the next campaign opened shows `ListAgents` returning

Campaign: kalaluthien/campaign-base#1
Repository: kalaluthien/campaign-base

`campaign-claim.py take` refuses every claim in campaign #1, so no sub-issue of it can be started. #187 Q1 landed a check (`1a3190b`, merged in `ced957f`) that a sub-issue's `Repository:` line must name a repository the campaign issue's `## Repos` lists, exempting only the literal `none`. Every sub-issue of #1 writes `Repository: kalaluthien/campaign-base` — the base itself — and #1's `## Repos` lists only `kalaluthien/agent-workspace`. Measured 2026-09-05 on `~/campaign-base` at `ced957f`: `scripts/campaign-claim.py take 1 190 member-commit-gate` exits 1 with

```
refusing: #190 says its work lands in kalaluthien/campaign-base, but campaign #1 lists kalaluthien/agent-workspace.
```

and #176, #187 and #190 all carry that same `Repository:` line, so this is every sub-issue of the campaign and not one body's typo. It shipped green because no case in `scripts/campaign-claim-test.py` ever puts the base's own name in a `Repository:` line: the fixture answers `Repository: none` on every passing path and `outside/scope` / `other/elsewhere` on the two scope cases, and the base's name is the one value for which the two readings differ.

Filed rather than patched because the answer is a decision, not a repair, and because it cannot be worked from inside the campaign either — a claim on *this* sub-issue is refused by the same rule. `issue_repo`'s own comment says "`none` resolves to the base, which is never in the list", which is the argument for the first reading:

- **The base is always in scope.** `## Repos` says which member repositories to clone when a campaign is opened; the base is cloned as its own member by a different route and no campaign lists it. Then `Repository: kalaluthien/campaign-base` is the same destination `none` names, and the scope check must exempt it. The code moves.
- **The base is a member like any other when a campaign changes it**, so `## Repos` lists it. The campaign issue body moves, which is a scope change and not an executor's write, and every existing campaign needs the same edit.

- Whichever is chosen, **a named case must fail when it is reverted, and that case must spell the base's own name in the `Repository:` line.** A fixture saying `none` cannot exhibit this defect and is what hid it.
- If the code moves, the site is the `if named is not None:` block in `cmd_take` (cite the function; `campaign-claim.py` is edited by several branches). `DEFAULT_REPO` is the base. Ship the allow case beside the refusal, since narrowing a refusal is what this is.
- If the body moves, `## Repos` gains a repository, which `opening-campaign` step 5 then acquires — check that acquiring the base into `<campaign>/repos/campaign-base/` is what already happens rather than a second, conflicting clone.
- Sweep for the other readers of the same premise: `check-campaign-claim.py` and `campaign-repos.py` both classify by repository, and any prose saying the base is never in `## Repos`.

Done when the merged pull request lets `campaign-claim.py take 1 <issue> <topic>` cut a ref for a sub-issue whose `Repository:` line names the base, with a named case that fails when the change is reverted, or the campaign issue bodies are corrected and a case pins the rule as written.

## Working it

This body is the whole brief, so this section is here on every sub-issue. It
points rather than restates: the rules are in the base's `AGENTS.md`, which a
delegate reaches through the `--add-dir <base>` its launch passes, and a second
copy of them here would be the one that goes stale.

- **A branch is already claimed on the remote for this sub-issue.** Its name is
  not written here — `gh issue create` mints the issue number, so the branch
  cannot be named in the body that creates it, and a placeholder nobody fills is
  worse than an absence. Read it with
  `scripts/campaign-claim.py live <N>`, which lists every claim of the campaign
  and where each is checked out. Check it out and work on it, and push every
  commit the moment it exists — a checkout that dies costs uncommitted work and
  nothing more.
- **Land by pull request against `main`**, opened on the first commit, body
  closing this issue with `Closes kalaluthien/campaign-base#<issue>`. Merge
  `origin/main` in before merging; resolve on the branch, never force-push.
- **You may land your own work**, and the three conditions that gate it are
  `AGENTS.md` § Merge conditions. One of them is a review you did not write, so
  **commission it yourself**: an in-process subagent, always, with the model and
  the level named — `AGENTS.md` § Review, and
  `.claude/skills/opening-campaign/references/reviewing.md` for the call.
- **The four messages** are `AGENTS.md` § The four messages. `REPORT` once when
  the pull request is open, unsolicited, naming its URL and the sha it sits at,
  **and ask for the review there**: a push retires any review before it and
  nobody is named to notice. If you ask and nothing comes, say so and stop — a
  silent wait reads exactly like work.
- **A fix round** is `AGENTS.md` § The fix round: reproduce each finding at the
  site it names before touching anything, and close the round with one `REPORT`
  plus a comment at that sha carrying one row per finding.
- **You do not write the campaign issue's body.** It is written at a scope
  change and at the close, and a sub-issue is neither.
